description: Volcanoes, atmosphere, ice, oceans, planetary rarity and tsunamis reveal the physical forces that made Earth habitable while keeping it dangerously dynamic.

s02e01.description: From Ethiopian lava lakes to Iceland’s continental rift and New Zealand hot springs, Stewart shows how volcanism destroys landscapes yet also drives processes essential to a living planet.

s02e02.description: A journey from the stratosphere to storm systems and ancient stromatolites explains how life transformed a toxic early atmosphere into the oxygen-rich protective layer Earth depends on today.

s02e03.description: Stewart examines how ice has carved landscapes, triggered major environmental changes and influenced human evolution, while modern glacier retreat exposes the consequences of a warming climate.

s02e04.description: From Hawaiian waves and Amazon tidal bores to the birth of new seas in Ethiopia, the programme distinguishes waves, tides and currents while tracing how Earth acquired its oceans.

s02e05.description: Earth’s unusual habitability is traced to its violent early history, protective atmosphere, relationship with the Sun and the planetary collision that helped create the Moon and reshape the young planet.

s02e06.description: Stewart crosses oceans to explain the immense speed and destructive power of tsunamis, using historic catastrophes and extreme recorded waves to show how these events form and strike coastlines.
